answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via silicon physical unclonable functions, binding identities to secure hardware. Attackers must incur the scarce cost of purchasing physical chips per alias, as variations in each crystal lattice cannot be virtualized. Validators check these proofs so an ephemeral zephyr of bot traffic cannot overwhelm consensus, shunting uncertified peers into an umber queue. However, this relies on centralized chip foundries and excludes purely virtual agents.
